headline_marked: [[Tabs in One]] organizes Chrome tabs into a single column, freeing up RAM
headline: Tabs in One organizes Chrome tabs into a single column, freeing up RAM
summary: Tired of Chrome's tab bar clutter and high RAM usage? This new extension consolidates all your tabs into a single, manageable column, then closes the originals to free up memory.
details: If you're reading this, you likely have over 40 tabs open in Chrome, consuming 4GB of RAM, making your laptop's fan whir, and preventing you from finding that one tab you opened minutes ago. The 'Tabs in One' extension aims to solve this exact problem.

Chrome's tab bar is horizontal. Once you have more than about 10 tabs, they shrink into tiny strips, making it impossible to see what's open, leading to duplicates and increased RAM usage. While tab managers exist, most have drawbacks.

Tabs in One collects all open tabs onto a single, clean, one-column page. When activated, each open tab is moved to this page, and the original tabs are closed, immediately freeing up RAM. You can restore any tab (or all) back to normal with a single click, without losing anything.
The extension requires permissions for tabs, storage, and context menus. It operates without an account, subscription, or any data leaving your browser, prioritizing user privacy.
Tabs in One is available on the Chrome Web Store and offers a one-week free trial. If it doesn't save you time, you can uninstall it at no cost.
